minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard the DPW director's 10-year capital plan; no votes taken, minutes postponed, plow-outsourcing analysis requested.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the DPW director present his 10-year capital request: equipment replacement, stormwater and culvert work, and cemetery projects. Members pressed on a second loader, cemetery funding, bundled requests, stormwater policy and whether to contract out plowing. Approval of the October 23 minutes was postponed for lack of voters, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment from the public; none was offered.
A cemetery commission representative asked how the commission could obtain a grant writer; chair suggested discussing it with the town manager.

votes.motion: Approval of the October 23 minutes was postponed to the next meeting for lack of members able to vote.
Motion to adjourn, with roll call vote
votes.outcome: passed; roll call of all four present members voting aye

budget_items.what_was_said: Director said the 10-year ask totals several million, about a million a year, with out years hard to predict.
figures_as_heard: almost a million dollars per year

budget_items.topic: Second front-end loader with plow (FY25 top priority)
budget_items.what_was_said: Director argued a second loader is needed for snow and backup; a member raised fleet-management concerns; existing loader near the engine-rebuild hours.
Engineer estimate compared with a similar recent project; grants or earmark possible.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery expansion funding and perpetual care
budget_items.what_was_said: Members questioned why cemetery capital isn't self-sustaining; perpetual care interest is small and plot prices were just raised.
Rental compared with purchase; bundled request, and members suggested it rank above cemetery expansion.
Request for a drainage fix for water entering a resident's driveway.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater overall and possible utility or fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said stormwater is straining the capital plan and discussed a comprehensive plan and a stormwater utility or impervious surface fee.
figures_as_heard: nearly a half a million dollars of project work every year

budget_items.what_was_said: Member said such one-time items belong in the operating budget, not the capital plan.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery hedge removal and stone wall
budget_items.what_was_said: Cemetery commission requested funds to replace hedges with a stone wall.
Members asked for a full-cost analysis of in-house versus contracted plowing, noting trucks already appropriated but not delivered.

budget_items.topic: Combination vacuum/jetter truck and contracted catch basin cleaning
budget_items.what_was_said: Combination truck not yet on the plan; contractor cleaning is costed per day.
Members said it should be operating budget with a bigger tree line.
Director said guardrail prices rose and it would be a future capital item.
Members mentioned typical hourly rates for grant writers.

decisions.decision: DPW director to return answers to member questions within a week or two, and the outsourced-plowing cost analysis by mid-January, sent to the whole committee and town manager.
A grant-opportunity assessment will be added to the capital package, especially for the first year.
Minutes of October 23 postponed to the next meeting.
Next meeting set for Monday November 20 at 7 o'clock, with schools on the agenda.
Members will each rank projects in a spreadsheet, the chair will collate a composite, and the committee will finalize ranking at a later meeting.
Planning board member will check with the stormwater task force representative and possibly ask the planning consultant for information on other communities, and report back.

what_happened.line: The DPW director presented a 10-year capital plan covering equipment replacement, stormwater and culvert work, and cemetery projects; no votes were taken.
Members pressed on a second front-end loader, cemetery funding, bundled requests, and whether in-house plowing costs less than contracting it out.
The DPW director is to return answers within a week or two and an outsourced-plowing cost analysis by mid-January.
Members said stormwater is straining the capital plan and discussed a comprehensive plan and a possible utility or impervious-surface fee.
Approval of the October 23 minutes was postponed to the next meeting, set for Monday November 20 with schools on the agenda.

why_it_matters: Capital requests like a second plow loader, drainage fixes and cemetery work compete for the same limited capital money, and what ranks high may reach a town meeting article.
A stormwater utility or impervious-surface fee, if pursued, would be a new charge on property owners, though it was only discussed here and nothing was decided.
